issues.legal_issue: A public servant may raise and have determined the objection that prior sanction was required before cognizance, without waiting for the stage of framing a charge.
material_facts: A public servant challenged the cognizance order on the ground that his alleged acts were connected with the discharge of official duty and that the required prior sanction had not been obtained.
The objection was raised before the case reached the stage of framing a charge.
issues.conclusion: The objection concerning the requirement of sanction may be raised and considered at any stage of the proceedings; the accused need not wait until the framing of charge.
issues.legal_principle: Section 197(1) of the Code of Criminal Procedure makes prior sanction a condition on the court’s jurisdiction to take cognizance where the alleged offence was committed while the public servant was acting or purporting to act in the discharge of official duty. In Suresh Kumar Bhikamchand Jain v. Pandey Ajay Bhushan, the Court held that an accused may produce legally considered materials to assist the court in correcting an exercise of jurisdiction it did not possess, and that the sanction question may be considered at any stage. Ashok Sahu v. Gokul Saikia held that the applicability of Section 197 must be judged at the earliest stage; P. Saha v. M.S. Kochar held that the question may be raised at any stage and that the court may consider all material on record. The direction in Birendra K. Singh v. State of Bihar that the objection could be raised only at the framing of charge does not state the correct law.

predicates.criminal_proceeding_against_public_serva: A criminal proceeding was initiated against a person serving as a public servant.
predicates.alleged_act_claimed_to_be_official: The accused claimed that the alleged act was done while acting or purporting to act in an official role.
predicates.sanction_objection_raised_before_charge: The accused raised the objection that prior approval was required before the case reached the framing of a charge.

issues.definition: When a public servant faces a criminal proceeding over an act claimed to have been done in an official role and raises the approval objection before charge, the objection may be considered at that stage.

issues.legal_issue: A public servant’s order to use force in carrying out an assigned official task may be connected to official duty where it is a response to an uncontrolled situation arising during that task.
material_facts: The public servant was appointed to carry out an order to remove an encroachment and attended the site with a police force for that purpose.
During the operation, an armed group threw stones and the situation became uncontrollable.
After giving a warning, the public servant ordered the police to fire to disperse the mob; one person died and two were injured.
The complaint alleged offences arising from the firing, and no prior sanction had been obtained.
issues.conclusion: The order to fire had a reasonable connection with the public servant’s assigned duty, so prior sanction was required before cognizance could be taken. As no sanction had been obtained, the cognizance and criminal proceeding against the public servant were quashed.
issues.legal_principle: Section 197(1) of the Code of Criminal Procedure bars cognizance without prior sanction when the alleged offence was committed while the public servant was acting or purporting to act in the discharge of official duty. Under Matajog Dobey v. H.C. Bhari, there must be a reasonable connection between the act and the duty, such that the public servant could reasonably, rather than fancifully, claim to have acted in the course of duty. Where a duty is imposed, it carries authority to do what is reasonably necessary to perform it. This principle was followed in Suresh Kumar Bhikamchand Jain v. Pandey Ajay Bhushan and Gauri Shankar Prasad v. State of Bihar. Applying it to the allegations, the order to fire was made in the course of the assigned operation to control the mob, and the absence of sanction made cognizance invalid.

predicates.criminal_complaint_against_public_servan: A criminal complaint was brought against a public servant for alleged offences.
predicates.official_order_to_carry_out_task: An authorized official directed the public servant to carry out a task.
predicates.official_task_was_reason_for_presence: The public servant attended the relevant location to carry out that assigned task.
predicates.mob_became_uncontrollable_during_task: A hostile crowd made the situation uncontrollable while the public servant was carrying out the task.
predicates.warning_given_before_force: The public servant gave a warning before force was used.
predicates.force_ordered_to_control_mob: The public servant ordered force for the purpose of controlling or dispersing the crowd.
predicates.no_prior_approval: The required prior approval had not been obtained.

issues.definition: When a complaint concerns a public servant who ordered force after an uncontrollable crowd obstructed an assigned task, despite a warning, and prior approval was absent, the proceeding against that public servant must be quashed.
